Something about John, the Apostle John, often called John the Revelator or John the Divine. In Matthew 4 Christ called James and John and they immediately left the ship and their father and followed him: once you're called, you are called. In the book of John, John doesn't often refer to himself as John; he refers to himself as the disciple whom Jesus loved, and the other apostles referred to him as he that lay on Christ's bosom, meaning wherever Christ was, John had his head right there trying to listen and learn. When everybody deserted Christ on the cross, John stuck by him, and Christ gave his mother to John: behold thy mother. John was on another level of love and admiration and dedication and loyalty. And when Christ told Peter, if I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee, Peter interpreted it as John never dying; John himself clears that up. What it really meant is Revelation 10:11: thou must prophesy again before many peoples and nations and tongues and kings. John will be regenerated and come back in the last days.

points: “And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness,” The Lord gave Christ for a witness to the people, a leader and commander of the people (Isaiah 55:4). “and the first begotten of the dead,” He was the first to rise from the dead, the firstfruits of them that slept (1 Corinthians 15:20), and by his resurrection from the dead we are begotten again unto a lively hope (1 Peter 1:3).

“Unto him that loved us,” That is the love Christ spoke of in John 15:9, as the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you. And that love goes right back to Deuteronomy 7:6-8: the Lord set his love upon us because of the oath he made with our ancestors, our forefathers. That is where that love comes from.

“and washed us from our sins in his own blood,” He is the one that washed us from our own wickedness. Our sins are not washed away because of our quote unquote good works. And the only way we overcome Satan and his minions, Esau, Edom, is by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of our testimony, the testimony God gave us concerning Christ, not our individual testimony (Revelation 12:11).

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

points: “I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos,” Patmos is a little island in the Aegean Sea, shaped like a seahorse. John of Patmos, also called John the Revelator, John the Divine, John the Theologian, is the John of Revelation, the apocalyptic text forming the final book of the New Testament. By most biblical historians he is considered exiled there as a result of anti-Christian persecution under the Roman emperor Domitian. Anti-Christian meaning what? Anti-Israelites keeping the commandments. Domitian was related to Titus and Vespasian, the younger brother of Titus, and he became emperor; that dude was wicked as hell. Since the Roman era, Christians and historians have considered the writer of Revelation to be the apostle John, John the Evangelist, supposed author of the Gospel of John.

“for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.” So he was banished there not for being a thief or a liar or a murderer, but for the word of God and for the testimony of Jesus Christ. He was exiled for the testimony of Christ, not for his own personal testimony.
